description: REQ-004's audit table row for `earn/clip/producer.sh` marks column (a) 'vulnerable pattern?' as 'n/a' and dismisses it with: 'run.sh (the real entrypoint) has no vulnerable pattern, so nothing downstream is at risk via this path.' This is factually inaccurate: producer.sh itself, independent of how it is invoked, contains the literal vulnerable preamble at its own line 22 (`set -a; . "$HOME/.openclaw/.env" 2>/dev/null; set +a`). The table's reasoning only checks whether producer.sh's usual caller (earn/clip/run.sh) is vulnerable, but does not check whether producer.sh itself re-sources the file and re-triggers the same clobber independent of the caller's own preamble. This matters concretely: skills/earn/clip-promote/run.sh's CLIP transition invokes `ANICCA_INSTANCE=clip-promote run_step ... bash "$HOME/anicca/skills/earn/clip/producer.sh" --url "$SRC_URL"` as a subprocess (skills/earn/clip-promote/run.sh:151) -- so any ANICCA_HOME correctly inherited by the caller up to that point is clobbered again by producer.sh's own independent sourcing before producer.sh's own script continues. The audit table's per-file disposition method (checking only the registry-entrypoint file, not every file in a call chain) is the same blind spot that let FIND-001's three files slip through the 'exhaustive' audit.

evidence.snippet:
set -uo pipefail
SKILLS="$HOME/.claude/skills/earn-clip-rewards/scripts"
...
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/_instance_paths.sh"
...
set -a; . "$HOME/.openclaw/.env" 2>/dev/null; set +a

| `earn/clip/producer.sh` | n/a (referenced by run.sh's comments, not itself the registry entrypoint) | run.sh (the real entrypoint) has no vulnerable pattern, so nothing downstream is at risk via this path | Not applicable. |
